name: Bottom of Cowley Falls
description:
Image Credit: @Wanderstories
Leader: Luen Warneke
Rated: Very Hard. Creek-based off-track, rugged terrain, very steep climbs.

Meeting: Please email the club for meeting point location. Please Note that this trip is an 3-4 hour drive from Townsville to the start point in the Tablelands. It might be a good idea to camp the previous night. 
Distance: ~5 km return
Duration: ~4-6 hours return

Walk Description:
Cowley Falls is located in Wooroonooran National Park and is a tall waterfall located close to the Palmerston Highway. The base of the falls has a small cave-like feature to it. We will walk along a rough track to Mitcha Creek to the top of the falls. Then we will back track and walk off-track, steeply down a ridgeline avoiding cliffs, stinging trees (Gympie Gympie), and wait-a-while to the base of the falls.

What to bring:
Day pack, food/snacks for the day, water 2 lt minimum (refill from creeks or carry 4 lt water), long sleeve clothing and good rugged footwear (to protect from sun, scratches, stings, and bites), electrolytes, insect repellent (leeches, mozzies), hat, sunscreen, personal first aid kit (basic), and sunglasses. Also, head torch and whistle. 

If you are uncomfortable using creek water for drinking water refill (after treating suitably), then carry 4 lt min for the day, or more to suit your requirements. Note that the club recommends that any natural water sources must be suitably treated before consumption.   

Fees: non-members $5

name: Killymoon Creek
description:
Leader: Molly Hoey

Rated: Hard  

Meeting: 7:00 am. Meeting place will be emailed closer to the time. Start and end location are on private property. Those accepted for the will be advised the location via email.

Distance: Approximately 7 kms round trip 

Walk Description:

Killymoon Creek, in the dry season, is a fantastic spot for rock-hopping enthusiasts. This walk start on a fire trail on private property with a few good hills to get everyone warmed up. The creek bed starts as a series of small rocky gullies which soon open up into a spectacular gorge.
We will have lunch at the swimming hole, where the polar bears amongst us can have a dip before lunch. This will be our turn around point and we will descend back down the creek from here.
This adventure will see us tackling numerous kinds of climbing. You will need to have a suitable level of fitness and coordination.

How long:
Full day walk. Estimate back at the car park around 4 pm.

What to bring:
Advised equipment: Water (at least 4L as we cannot guarantee suitable water from the creek), Lunch (Snacks and electrolytes), Basic first aid, suitable sun safe clothing, sun screen, Mozzie spray and suitable shoes.

Speciality equipment: I strongly advise gloves as this walk requires a lots of hand work (but that’s just personal preference). You will need boots with plenty of tread for grip.
Non Member fee - 5$

 Must be over 18yrs to participate.
